spikes.question: Which code path owns the review-run false-stale, how broad is the blast radius (only wrapper-root + custom storyDir?), and is a clean, backward-compatible two-sided metadataRoot fix feasible?
spikes.note: Owned by core/review-run.ts + handlers/review-run.ts; no in-repo disposable code carried forward.
spikes.result: Root cause: review-run computes AND re-checks material/story hashes from signedWorkspaceRoot instead of the resolved metadataRoot; loadConfig(metadataRoot) is what knows the custom storyDir, so on a wrapper-root layout the storyDir metadata is wrongly folded into both hashes. The buildReviewRunWorkspaceBinding fallback is dead because the handler always passes a precomputed storyFilesHash. Scope: strictly wrapper-root (metadataRoot != gitRoot) + non-default storyDir; plain repos and default storyDir unaffected (metadataRoot defaults to gitCwd; default metadata prefixes hardcoded). Fix (clean, backward-compatible): (1) thread metadataRoot into captureReviewRunSnapshot + diagnoseReviewRunSnapshot, pass workspace.metadataRoot||ctx.root from the handler with metadataRoot defaulting to projectRoot for byte-identical plain repos; (2) thread run.workspaceBinding?.metadataRoot ?? projectRoot into the two consumer freshness calls (binding already persists metadataRoot; legacy runs fall back to projectRoot). done-oracle/done-prepare/verifier already thread a distinct metadataRoot, so review-run is the lone outlier. Regression guard mandatory: prove plain/default byte-identical and lock the wrapper-root + custom-storyDir path.
